farraa:1-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلتِّينِ وَٱلزَّيْتُونِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: It is this fig of yours and this olive of yours. It is also said: they are two mountains in Syria (al-Shām). And he said on another occasion: two mosques in Syria, one of them being the one on which Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, spoke to Moses ﷺ. Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard [143/a] a man from the people of Syria, who was a man of tafsīr, say: «التين» is the mountains between Ḥulwān and Hamadhān, and «الزيتون» is the mountains of Syria. ﴿وَطُورِ سِينِينَ﴾: a mountain.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهَـٰذَا ٱلْبَلَدِ ٱلأَمِينِ﴾.
Mecca. He means: الآمِن (the secure). The Arabs say «الأمين» for «الآمن». The poet said:
ألم تعْلى يا أسْم ويْحكِ أننى * حَلفتُ يميناً لا أخون أمينى؟
(Do you not know, O Asmāʾ — woe to you! — that I have sworn an oath not to betray the one who trusts me [lit. my secure one]?)
He means: آمنى (the one who is safe with me). [Translator's note: «تعْلى» is as printed; presumably «تعلمي».]

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِيۤ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾.
He says: We bring the son of Adam to the best of his form, which is his upright proportion and the full maturity of his youth, which is the best he ever is; then after that We return him to the most decrepit age. Although it [Translator's note: i.e. «الإنسان»] is singular, what is meant by it is: We do this with many people. The Arabs say: أَنْفَق ماله على فلان (he spent his wealth on so-and-so), when he spent only part of it; and this is frequent in the Revelation. Among it is His word concerning Abū Bakr: ﴿الَّذِى يُؤْتِى مَالَهُ يَتَزَكَّى﴾; He did not mean all of his wealth; He meant only part of it.

farraa:5-5.t:
And it is said: ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَاهُ أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ﴾.
To the Fire. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿إِلاَّ الذين آمنوا﴾, an exception from «الإنسان», because the meaning of «الإنسان» is "the many". Similar to it is: ﴿إِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ، إِلاَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is "أسفل السافلين". Had it been أسفل سافل, it would have been correct, because the wording of «الإنسان» is singular; but «سافلين» was said in the plural because «الإنسان» has a plural meaning. You say: هذا أفضل قائم (this is the best one standing), but you do not say: هذا أفضل قائمين, because you are referring by implication to a single person. When a single individual is not what is aimed at, its noun may be referred back to in the singular and in the plural, as in His word: ﴿والَّذِى جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وصَدَّقَ بِهِ أُولَئكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُون﴾, and He said in ʿAin Sīn Qāf [Translator's note: Sūrat al-Shūrā]: ﴿وإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَإِنَّ الإِنْسَانَ كَفُورٌ﴾, so He referred «الإنسان» back to a plural, and referred «تصبهم» back to «الإنسان», for the reason I have told you.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَا يُكَذِّبُكَ﴾ [143/b].
He says: what is it that makes you disbelieve that people will be requited for their deeds? As if He said: who then can call you a liar regarding reward and punishment, after what has become clear to him of Our creating man as We have described?
